items.text: 7 mistakes costing you over £200 a year on fuel - from boot clutter to missed tyre checks
items.article: Kevin Booker who holds six Guinness World Records for 'efficient driving' has revealed everyday tips that could save you vital cash at the pumps As diesel prices hit an all-time high and petrol continues to soar, help is here. A bloke who holds six Guinness World Records for “efficient driving” has revealed everyday tips that could save the average driver around £200 a year on fuel. Some 62% of Brits have cut back on their driving to save cash due the spiralling cost of living this year, while 63% now only drive when necessary, Dacia research found. But Kevin Booker, from Wales, who has a total of six Guinness World Records for fuel-efficient driving, or 'hypermiling’, has revealed the simple mistakes many of us are making. He tested his tips in the Dacia Duster Journey hybrid 155 and managed 79 miles per gallon real-world driving – compared with its official economy figure of 61.4mpg. The hybrid 155 combines a petrol engine with two electric motors, for optimum performance, and is priced from £21,845 new. On Monday (28 September), diesel prices hit an all-time high of 199.18p per litre, according to the RAC, with petrol costing 174.13p. The RAC said diesel prices had entered ‘uncharted territory’ and served as a reminder of "just how exposed the UK is". A Dacia spokesperson said: “People can’t control the price at the pump, but simple changes to how they drive and maintain their car can help each tank go further.”

items.text: Got a tip for us? Here's how to submit
items.article: If you want to provide news tips or documents to The Wall Street Journal, there are several ways to do so. It’s still possible for tipsters to reach out directly to our reporters by phone or email if they feel comfortable doing so. The tools outlined below can help you communicate more securely, and in some cases, anonymously, though no strategy is foolproof. Keep in mind: the most useful news tips are detailed, provide some documentation and suggest names of people the Journal might contact to verify the information. If you want a reply from someone at the Journal, please select a secure way to do so from the choices below. Messages will be checked on a regular basis but replies could be delayed. Please note that the Journal may not respond to all messages. Use these tools at your own risk and after reviewing the terms and instructions provided by the app developers. Send us a letter or a parcel. Address it to: Marcelo Prince, investigations editor The Wall Street Journal 1211 Avenue of the Americas, 6th floor New York, NY 10036 For greater anonymity, don’t put a return address on the outside of the envelope. Instead, consider putting your return address inside the envelope or providing a Signal phone number for us to contact you.

items.article: Labour's Andy Burnham has confirmed the removal of VAT from electricity bills starts today, part of a combined £345 boost for households amid the cost of living crisis Andy Burnham has confirmed energy bill tax cuts from TODAY for households. The Labour Party government's Mr Burnham, Chancellor John Healey and Energy Secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, have announced the scrapping of VAT from electricity bills begins today. The HMRC tax reduction will assist households with their energy costs by removing roughly £45 from the annual Ofgem price cap and forms part of the Prime Minister's broader strategy for 'everyday fixes' to provide families with some relief. Mr Burnham stated the £45 reduction "builds" on the £150 of expenses removed from energy bills in the Budget last year and "expansion of the £150 Warm Home Discount" to approximately six million households - totalling a £345 boost overall. Mr Burnham said: "For many families, the energy bill is the one they dread the most. I don't accept that it has to be this way, and I am determined to bring down costs for good. "But I know people can't wait. Families need breathing space now. That's why, from today, VAT is gone from your electricity bill. And we're going further, capping bus fares at £2 from January and cutting business rates for pubs, social clubs and live music venues.", reports Birmingham Live . items.article: Vaping could cost users £600 more a year from today, as the Government introduces new taxes in a bid to create a 'smoke-free generation'. Published: 02:00, 1 October 2026 | Updated: 09:29, 1 October 2026 Vaping could cost users £600 more a year from today, under a new tax crackdown aimed at creating a 'smoke-free generation'. A new levy of £2.20 per 10ml of vape liquid means a heavy user getting through around 270 bottles a year could face the £600 annual hit, while a bottle currently marketed at around £3.99 could now cost almost £7. Smokers will also be hit, with a 44p rise on a typical pack of 20 cigarettes – equivalent to around £160 a year for someone smoking a pack a day. Combined with other duty increases, the overall rise is expected to be about £1.20 a pack, which could see heavy smokers spending an extra £440 a year. A typical 50g pouch of tobacco is also expected to rise by around £4.20, amounting to almost £110 extra a year for someone getting through a pouch every fortnight – or £218 for those buying one a week.

Gov. Gavin Newsom on Wednesday signed the Plug and Play Solar Act, a bill by Sen. Scott Wiener that will allow anyone — renter or homeowner — to set small panels on their patios or fences and plug them directly into wall outlets without having to navigate any utility permissions. “This law and the small solar panels it unlocks put people, including renters, in charge of their energy bills,” Wiener said in a statement. The systems — also called “balcony solar” — are already popular in Germany and at least nine other U.S. states have legalized them.
